title: Which distribution moved?
description: Compare competing explanations against contract, input, label, and performance evidence before choosing a cause.

diagnoses.label: Data quality incident
diagnoses.detail: A schema, unit, join, timestamp, or upstream transformation broke its contract.

diagnoses.label: Covariate shift
diagnoses.detail: P(X) moved while the input-to-outcome relationship is still assumed stable.

diagnoses.label: Prior probability shift
diagnoses.detail: P(Y) moved while within-class input patterns are still assumed stable.

diagnoses.label: Concept drift
diagnoses.detail: P(Y|X) changed, so the same input evidence now implies a different outcome.

scenarios.label: New camera fleet
scenarios.context: A visual inspection model receives traffic from a newly installed camera generation.
scenarios.summary: The device change moved input appearance, but the available labels do not show a changed defect relationship.
scenarios.nextProbe: Collect enough labeled images from the new cameras and compare slice-level recall before adapting the model.

evidence.label: Image contract
evidence.detail: Types, dimensions, and preprocessing version match the registered contract.

evidence.label: Brightness KS distance
evidence.detail: The new camera pipeline produces a materially different brightness distribution.

evidence.label: New-device traffic
evidence.detail: The population mix changed at the same time as the alert.

evidence.label: Labeled recall
evidence.detail: Only a small labeled sample has arrived, so harm is not established yet.

whyNot.data-quality-incident: The registered image contract and preprocessing version still pass; no broken field or transformation is visible.
whyNot.covariate-shift: Input appearance and population mix moved together. Treat stable P(Y|X) as a hypothesis to validate with labels.
whyNot.label-shift: There is not yet evidence that defect prevalence changed while within-class images remained stable.
whyNot.concept-drift: Concept drift requires labeled evidence that the relationship between image patterns and defects changed.

scenarios.label: Holiday fraud spike
scenarios.context: A payment model sees a sudden increase in confirmed fraud during a holiday weekend.
scenarios.summary: Confirmed fraud prevalence rose while labeled within-class score shapes and ranking remain close to the reference.
scenarios.nextProbe: Re-estimate calibration and decision thresholds on confirmed outcomes while monitoring whether within-class patterns remain stable.

evidence.label: Feature contract
evidence.detail: No schema, freshness, or upstream release anomaly is present.

evidence.label: Confirmed fraud rate
evidence.detail: Outcome prevalence increased in joined chargeback labels.

evidence.label: Within-class score shape
evidence.detail: Score distributions conditional on the confirmed class remain close.

evidence.label: Labeled AUROC
evidence.detail: Ranking quality is approximately preserved despite changed prevalence.

whyNot.data-quality-incident: Contracts and freshness are healthy, and the movement appears in confirmed outcomes rather than one malformed feature.
whyNot.covariate-shift: The strongest evidence is changed outcome prevalence, not a broad movement in unlabeled inputs.
whyNot.label-shift: The positive rate moved while labeled ranking and within-class score shapes remain approximately stable.
whyNot.concept-drift: The available labeled evidence does not show that the input-to-outcome relationship materially changed.

scenarios.label: New approval policy
scenarios.context: A lending policy changed which applications receive manual review, altering observed outcomes for familiar applicants.
scenarios.summary: Inputs and prevalence are close to reference, but labeled calibration and error rates changed after the policy intervention.
scenarios.nextProbe: Build a representative post-policy labeled window and test a candidate against both current and protected historical slices.

evidence.label: Feature contract
evidence.detail: The data pipeline and feature definitions are unchanged.

evidence.label: Input domain classifier AUC
evidence.detail: Reference and current inputs are difficult to distinguish.

evidence.label: Positive outcome rate
evidence.detail: Overall prevalence is close to the reference window.

evidence.label: Calibration error
evidence.detail: For similar scores, observed outcomes now differ after the policy change.

whyNot.data-quality-incident: The contract remains healthy and the change aligns with a real decision-policy intervention.
whyNot.covariate-shift: Input distributions remain close, while labeled score-to-outcome behavior moved.
whyNot.label-shift: Overall outcome prevalence is stable; the conditional relationship changed within an affected slice.
whyNot.concept-drift: Labeled calibration changed for similar inputs after a policy intervention, supporting changed P(Y|X).

scenarios.label: Latency unit regression
scenarios.context: A risk feature jumps immediately after an upstream telemetry deployment.
scenarios.summary: A source release changed milliseconds to microseconds without updating the registered feature contract.
scenarios.nextProbe: Roll back or repair the source, identify affected records, and replay the monitor before considering any model change.

evidence.label: Valid feature range
evidence.detail: Values exceed the contract by roughly three orders of magnitude.

evidence.label: Upstream version
evidence.detail: The distribution jump begins exactly at the telemetry rollout.

evidence.label: Other feature families
evidence.detail: The incident is isolated to one transformed field.

evidence.label: High-risk predictions
evidence.detail: The malformed feature drives a large prediction shift.

whyNot.data-quality-incident: A contract violation starts exactly at an upstream release and explains the prediction movement.
whyNot.covariate-shift: This is not a trustworthy population change; the measurement unit broke.
whyNot.label-shift: No outcome evidence indicates a prevalence change, and the malformed input explains the alert.
whyNot.concept-drift: Retraining on the malformed unit would encode the defect instead of restoring the intended relationship.
